comments.text: Great video, Geoff. One criticism: my family moved to Lopez in 1973. I graduated from Lopez Island Consolidated School in 1975. I still have two siblings and relatives and friends living there and was last there myself [on San Juan in Friday Harbor and Roche Harbor] in August of 2024. At NO TIME in ALL of those years [53] were "most of the roads" on Lopez, Orcas or San Juan "dirt". Driveways, yes or more likely gravel. But the entire county has quite good roads and has since before the 70's and probably even before that [nobody ever said "Well, it used to be TERRIBLE!]. Even Shaw has a hard surface road and it has ZERO public services for visitors. However, you are absolutely right. It was hard for my mom and stepdad and then my sibs to make a living "on the rock" and 3 of the 5 of us kids left. My brother is an electrician there [just retiring] and only managed to have a home because he had a great client who sold him part of her property in lieu of being paid for his labor when she built a big house on her remaining land. My sister married the son of the math teacher/soccer coach [and the 1st/2nd grade teacher was his wive] and he became a plumber [and he's retired from that and now works at the grocery store to make ends meet] and she still teaches tap dancing and now lives in a house my father built [he was also an electrician, but in CA] "just so that it doesn't stand empty all year when he's not there" and pays for utilities and upkeep. But it is extremely difficult for young people to afford living on Lopez. You also failed to mention the issue of the the State Ferry service. That's the only way to get a car on/off the Island and the fare is $36.15 for a car and driver, $18 for each add'l passenger [$9 for seniors, $0 for children under 18] and takes an HOUR each way and there are only 4 sailings each way in the WINTER with more in the SUMMER but they're MUCH MORE CROWDED in the summer too. Miss a ferry on either end, either because you're LATE or it is FULL and you get to WAIT for about 4 hours, or even overnight. A "trip to Costco" is an all day excursion. Most people just shop on the island because it isn't worth the time and hassle to do more than one trip off per month and most people don't even try to leave in the summer season [Memorial Day to Indigenous People's Day].

The most grandiose waterfall in Earth's history is located here... but it does not have a single drop of water. 
When the narrator mentions at 4:45 that Washington State's geography was heavily carved by the Cordilleran ice sheet during the last Ice Age, it sets the stage for a much more violent geological cataclysm nearby. When the ice dam holding back the colossal glacial Lake Missoula ruptured, a volume of water exceeding all modern rivers on the planet combined unleashed across Washington State. Traveling at a devastating 130 km/h, this mega-flood literally stripped away the Earth's crust. This apocalyptic event sculpted Dry Falls, a gigantic crescent-shaped stone cliff measuring 5.5 kilometers wide and 120 meters high! It is 5 times wider and 2.5 times taller than Niagara Falls. Standing on the edge of this canyon today, you are looking at the bare, silent skeleton of the most gigantic waterfall in the known history of our planet, which dried up thousands of years ago. 😱

replies.text: There were many Missoula Floods, not just one.
